Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

WINNENDEN, Germany (CNN) -- Students jumped out of windows and locked themselves in classrooms as a former pupil rampaged through a German school with a gun, killing at least a dozen people there Wednesday, a student at the school told CNN. People lay flowers at the school Wednesday. "Suddenly there were police standing in front of me and told us to run outside quickly," Luisa Santonastaso, 16, said. "At first we didn't know what to do. So first we went to the class and picked up some of our classmates and ran out. "Then we heard that someone was inside shooting. Then we also saw a teacher who had blood on his hands because he wanted to help a female teacher who sacrificed herself for a student -- she stood in front of a student to protect her," the girl told CNN by phone from Germany. "The guy just entered the classroom and started shooting and a friend of mine was panicking so much that she jumped out of a window. I think she broke her arm. She's in hospital now." Santonastaso's friend was not the only one who jumped, she said. Dressed in military gear, the gunman -- identified by police as Tim Kretschmer, 17 -- killed a total of 15 people in two different towns before he died.  Watch more about the shootings » . Initial indications are that he shot himself, but police are continuing to investigate, said Erwin Hetger, the regional chief of police. The rampage in Winnenden, a small town about 20 kilometers (12 miles) northeast of Stuttgart, and spread to neighboring Wendlingen. As people at Albertville-Realschule Winnenden school -- where Kretschmer used to be a student -- realized what was happening, many burst into tears, Santonastaso said. "Everybody was crying because nobody could really imagine what had just happened. They brought us to the swimming pool hall in Winnenden for security reasons," she said. "Then all our parents were called because no child was allowed to leave without parents," she continued. At least one parent got awful news when she arrived. "One mother came and the teachers had to tell her that her child had been injured or shot dead, and then she cried really hard and fainted," Santonastaso said. iReport.com: Town in shock over shooting . Santonastaso's own parents were more fortunate. "When I first called to tell them what had happened they wanted to come right away, but I told them that wasn't possible because we were being brought to somewhere safe," she said. Later, she said: "My parents and my friend came and we went out with them. Out there it got a bit better." CNN's Marco Woldt and Lianne Turner contributed to this report .

People laid flowers at the school Wednesday.

“Suddenly there were police standing in front of me, and they told us to run outside quickly,” said Luisa Santonastaso, 16. “At first we didn’t know what to do. So first we went to the class and picked up some of our classmates and ran out.

“Then we heard that someone was inside shooting. Then we also saw a teacher who had blood on his hands because he wanted to help a female teacher who sacrificed herself for a student—she stood in front of a student to protect her,” the girl told CNN by phone from Germany.

“The guy just entered the classroom and started shooting, and a friend of mine was panicking so much that she jumped out of a window. I think she broke her arm. She’s in hospital now.”

Santonastaso said her friend was not the only person who jumped.

Dressed in military-style gear, the gunman—identified by police as 17-year-old Tim Kretschmer—killed a total of 15 people in two different towns before he died.

Initial indications suggest he shot himself, but police are continuing to investigate, said Erwin Hetger, the regional chief of police.

The rampage began in Winnenden, a small town about 20 kilometers, or 12 miles, northeast of Stuttgart, and spread to neighboring Wendlingen.

As people at Albertville-Realschule Winnenden—the school Kretschmer had once attended—realized what was happening, many burst into tears, Santonastaso said.

“Everybody was crying because nobody could really imagine what had just happened. They brought us to the swimming pool hall in Winnenden for security reasons,” she said.

“Then all our parents were called because no child was allowed to leave without parents,” she continued.

At least one parent received devastating news when she arrived.

“One mother came and the teachers had to tell her that her child had been injured or shot dead, and then she cried really hard and fainted,” Santonastaso said.

Santonastaso’s own parents were more fortunate.

“When I first called to tell them what had happened, they wanted to come right away, but I told them that wasn’t possible because we were being brought to somewhere safe,” she said.

Later, she added: “My parents and my friend came, and we went out with them. Out there, it got a bit better.”

CNN’s Marco Woldt and Lianne Turner contributed to this report.
outputs.L2:
WINNENDEN, Germany (CNN) — A student at a German school told CNN that pupils leapt from windows and barricaded themselves inside classrooms Wednesday after a former student opened fire on campus, killing at least 12 people there. Flowers were placed at the school on Wednesday.

“Out of nowhere, police were in front of me, telling us to get outside fast,” said Luisa Santonastaso, 16. “At first, we didn’t know how to react. We went to the classroom first, gathered some classmates, and then ran out.

“After that, we heard there was someone inside shooting. We also saw a teacher with blood on his hands because he had tried to help a female teacher who sacrificed herself for a student — she stepped in front of the student to shield her,” Santonastaso told CNN by telephone from Germany.

“The man came into the classroom and began firing. One of my friends was so terrified that she jumped through a window. I think she broke her arm. She’s in the hospital now.”

Santonastaso said her friend was not the only person who jumped from a window.

Police identified the gunman as 17-year-old Tim Kretschmer. Wearing military-style clothing, he killed 15 people in all across two towns before he died.

Early evidence suggests Kretschmer shot himself, though investigators are still examining the circumstances, regional police chief Erwin Hetger said.

The attack began in Winnenden, a small town roughly 20 kilometers, or 12 miles, northeast of Stuttgart, and later extended to nearby Wendlingen.

At Albertville-Realschule Winnenden, the school Kretschmer had once attended, students began crying as they understood what was unfolding, Santonastaso said.

“Everyone was crying because no one could really believe what had just happened. For safety, they took us to the swimming pool hall in Winnenden,” she said.

“Then they called all of our parents, because no child was allowed to leave unless their parents came,” she added.

For at least one parent, the news on arrival was devastating.

“One mother came, and the teachers had to tell her that her child had been injured or shot dead. She cried very hard and then fainted,” Santonastaso said.

Santonastaso’s parents were luckier.

“When I first phoned them to say what had happened, they wanted to come immediately, but I told them they couldn’t because we were being taken somewhere safe,” she said.

Later, she added, “My parents and my friend arrived, and we left with them. Once we were outside, things felt a little better.”

CNN’s Marco Woldt and Lianne Turner contributed to this report.
